pages.title: Let's meet

questions.label: What is your full name?
questions.help: Use your full name as you normally write it, in any language.

questions.label: What is your company, organization, or professional name?
Which email address should we use for your project?
questions.help: A personal email is fine. We will use this address for project communication.

questions.label: What phone number can we contact you on?
questions.help: Include your country calling code, for example +91. A reachable number is needed if you choose phone or a phone-based messaging service.

pages.description: Tell us who you are and the name we should use for your project.

pages.title: How we should work with you

questions.label: What is your role in this project?
Where are you based?
questions.help: No home address is needed. Check the suggested timezone and change it if needed.

questions.label: How would you prefer us to communicate?
questions.help: We will confirm available channels with you. You can add your preferred language and contact window.

questions.label: In a few sentences, what does your business or organization do?
questions.placeholder: We repair equipment for local businesses and want customers to request service online.

questions.label: Which industry or field best describes your work?
questions.help: Choose more than one if needed, or describe your field and niche.

questions.label: What stage is the business at?
What do you provide, and how do people receive it?
questions.help: Choose every model relevant to this project. This helps us show the right questions.

questions.label: What are the main products, services, or activities we should focus on first?
questions.help: Start with up to three examples, or share a catalog or document link. Detailed records can follow later.

questions.label: Where do you currently serve people, and where do you want to serve them next?
questions.help: Describe current and planned markets separately. It is fine if expansion is undecided.

questions.label: Who is the main customer or user we should prioritize?
questions.help: Describe their main need or situation. Internal tools can prioritize employees or partners.

questions.label: Is the person using your offer also the person choosing and paying for it?
questions.help: If they are different, add the roles—for example buyer, user, manager, or purchasing team.

questions.label: What usually makes someone need your offer, and what makes them hesitate?
questions.help: One recent customer example is enough.

pages.title: Why you are starting this project

questions.label: Why do you want Starter Shifter's help now?
questions.help: Tell us what prompted the project and the main problem with your current situation.

questions.label: What would you most like this project to improve?
questions.help: Choose up to three improvements, then mark your first priority.

questions.label: What result would make this project worthwhile to you?
presets: Help us set a realistic target
questions.help: Add a measurable outcome and review date if you know them. Your target is a starting point to discuss.

questions.label: Where can we see your current business online?
questions.help: Website, store, social profiles, marketplace, directory listing, or demo links are welcome.

questions.label: How does one typical customer request or internal task move from start to finish?
questions.help: Describe one example or share a document link. A new business can describe its intended process.

questions.label: Where does that process take the most effort or go wrong?
questions.help: You can add anything you have tried that should be retained or avoided.

questions.label: Which parts of the business should this project help with?
questions.help: Choose the work you need. Requests will be reviewed against your agreed scope; selections do not change your plan or price.

questions.label: What should people be able to do when this is ready?
What must be ready for the first launch, and what can wait?
questions.help: Start with up to three launch priorities. You can also note anything explicitly excluded.

pages.title: Your market and reasons to choose you

questions.label: Who or what would people choose if they did not choose you?
questions.help: Up to three competitors, marketplaces, manual alternatives, or doing nothing. Names or links are enough.

questions.label: Why do people choose you, or why do you hope they will?
questions.help: Tell us which strengths exist today and which differences you are planning.

questions.label: What evidence or insights could help us understand your market and customers?
questions.help: Share links to reviews, redacted feedback, research, sales patterns, seasonal demand, or support themes. Note the source, date, and permission for public proof where known. Do not share raw private records.

questions.label: What brand and business content do you already have?
questions.help: Mark each asset as ready, needs updating, or needs help. Final files can be shared securely later.

questions.label: How should your business feel and sound to people?
questions.help: Add language preferences, styles to avoid, or up to two reference links and what you like about them.

questions.label: Who can supply or approve the content we will need?
questions.help: Use an existing contact or give a person or role. A shared folder link and expected availability are optional. Content production and licensing need an agreed scope.

questions.label: Do your products, services, or users have any special restrictions or approval requirements?
questions.help: Add a short description where useful. Do not share sensitive records.

questions.label: Will the project handle private information or different levels of access?
questions.help: Select categories only. Do not upload customer, patient, or employee records.

questions.label: Are there language, accessibility, device, or connectivity needs we should design around?
questions.help: You can add the languages, devices, or specific needs you already know.

questions.label: Is there a target launch date or event we should plan around?
questions.help: If the date is fixed, add the reason or event. This records your request; timing will be agreed with you.

questions.label: What investment limits should guide our recommendations?
questions.help: Use an amount or range and a currency. Keep project fees, tools/support, and advertising separate. Agreed charges come from your project records.

questions.label: What could affect your ability to launch or respond to us?

pages.title: Your website's job

questions.label: Are we creating something new, improving what you have, or replacing it?
questions.help: We can reuse the existing website link you shared earlier.

questions.label: What information or features must visitors find before taking the main action you selected?
Do you have a platform preference or an existing platform we must keep?
questions.help: Add the plan name or any reason we must keep a platform, if known.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Website ownership and content

questions.label: Do you already own the domain and website/hosting accounts?
questions.help: Add the provider and account owner if known. Never share passwords or credentials here.

questions.label: Which pages or content must be ready at launch?
questions.placeholder: For example: Home — ready, Services — needs writing
questions.help: Add your priority launch pages or a link to an existing sitemap. Mark content as ready, needs writing, or needs review.

questions.label: What needs preserving from your existing online presence?
questions.help: Add anything important to preserve. Content or data that needs moving can be discussed in the migration step.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Product catalog

questions.label: Approximately how many products and variations should launch first?
questions.help: Count products and variations for your first launch. Variations might be size, color, material, or configuration.

questions.label: What must customers choose or provide for a product?
questions.help: You can add one example after choosing the relevant options.

questions.label: Where are the current product details, prices, and images kept?
questions.help: Share the current catalog link, document link, or tool name. A full catalog can follow later; use only redacted examples.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Stock and availability

questions.label: Where do you track stock or availability today?
questions.help: Add the tool name and the person who keeps the source up to date, if known.

questions.label: Which locations and sales channels share that stock?
questions.placeholder: For example: 2 stores and an online shop
questions.help: An approximate location count and your main sales channels are enough. Mention reservations, batches/expiry, or serial numbers only if relevant.

questions.label: What should happen when availability changes or counts disagree?
questions.help: Add who checks exceptions if known. Detailed stock rules can follow later.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Delivery, pickup, and returns

questions.label: How do orders reach customers, and where can you deliver?
questions.help: Add your delivery areas and any excluded regions.

questions.label: Which providers and delivery rules do you already use?
questions.help: An existing document link is welcome. Include providers, rates, packaging constraints, processing time, tracking, and exceptions only if known.

questions.label: Who handles dispatch problems, returns, exchanges, and refunds?
questions.help: Name the responsible person or team and link or summarize your policy. Add who pays return or replacement costs if known.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Supplier-made or personalized products

questions.label: Which suppliers produce or send your products?
questions.placeholder: Supplier or production team — name or link
questions.help: Add supplier names or links and whether they are selected or still being considered. Include your own production team if relevant.

questions.label: What must be approved before an order enters production?
questions.help: Add whether the quality and timing have already been tested.

questions.label: Who handles supplier failures or remakes, and when must the supplier be paid?
questions.help: Add who handles failed production or incorrect personalization, production deadlines, and any payment-before-payout constraints, if known.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Bookings and appointments

questions.label: What can people book, and what limits availability?
questions.placeholder: For example: 30-minute online consultations with one adviser
questions.help: Start with one service or an existing schedule link. Mention duration, staff or resource, location or online delivery, and capacity if known.

questions.label: How should a booking be confirmed?
questions.help: Optionally add your calendar and any information needed before booking.

questions.label: What should happen if someone reschedules, cancels, or does not attend?
questions.help: Link or summarize your policy. Mention deposits and reminders if relevant.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Quotes, projects, and B2B buying

questions.label: What information do you need to decide whether an inquiry is a good fit?
questions.help: Choose the information needed to qualify a request. You may also share a sample inquiry form link.

questions.label: How does an inquiry become an approved order or project?
questions.help: A short description or existing template link is enough. Include quotes, approvers, contracts or purchase orders, milestones, and handoffs where relevant.

questions.label: Are there customer-specific prices or purchasing rules?

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Digital products and learning

questions.label: What digital content will people receive, and how is it delivered?
questions.help: Add the format and how people receive it, if already decided.

questions.label: What controls who can access or use it?
questions.help: Choose the controls you need and add any known limits.

questions.label: What should happen after access is granted?

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Subscriptions and memberships

questions.label: What recurring value does each membership or subscription provide?
questions.help: Tell us the ongoing benefit people receive, or share an existing offer link. Add tiers and billing intervals only if defined.

questions.label: How should trials, renewals, upgrades, or failed payments work?
questions.help: These are choices to discuss. Add your existing rules or preferred behavior; never share payment credentials.

questions.label: What happens when someone pauses or cancels?
questions.help: Link or summarize your policy. Mention when access ends, outstanding deliveries, refunds, and known reasons people leave.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Marketplaces and multiple providers

questions.label: Which groups use the platform, and what does each group need to do?
questions.help: Add what each selected group needs to do.

questions.label: How are providers approved and transactions allocated?
questions.help: Include provider quality checks and who supplies the product or performs the service.

questions.label: Who collects money, pays providers, and resolves disputes?
questions.help: Describe money collection, provider payouts, commissions, refunds, and dispute ownership only where relevant.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Internal team workflows

questions.label: Which repeated staff task should we improve first?
questions.help: Build on the workflow you already described. Add frequency or time spent only if known.
presets: Help us choose the priority task

questions.label: Who should submit, approve, edit, and view that work?
questions.help: For each relevant role, add whether they submit, approve, edit, or view work. Mention exceptions and a history of changes if needed.

questions.label: What would help the team adopt the new process?

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Customer payments and invoicing

questions.label: How should your customers pay, and in which currencies?
questions.help: Add the currencies your customers should use. This concerns your customer payments, separate from paying Starter Shifter.

questions.label: Do you already have payment and accounting providers?
questions.help: Add provider names and whether the accounts are approved, if known. Mention any invoicing connection. Never share bank or card credentials.

questions.label: What approved pricing, tax, invoice, and refund rules must the flow follow?
questions.help: Link the approved rules or name the person who will confirm pricing, taxes, invoices, and refunds.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Your social presence

questions.label: Which social channels should we set up or improve first?
questions.help: Choose up to three priorities. Add existing handles, account owner, and access status without sharing logins.

questions.label: What should your social content help people understand or do?
Who will create, approve, and publish content?
questions.help: Optionally add available formats and your preferred cadence. Ongoing content production depends on the agreed scope.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Campaign and growth priorities

questions.label: Which offer and audience should a campaign focus on first?
questions.help: Use the offer, audience, and goals already shared. Add only the narrower first campaign priority.
presets: Help us choose the campaign priority

questions.label: How do people currently find you, and what has worked or failed?
questions.help: Optionally add what worked or failed and an existing results link.

questions.label: What limits should guide campaign spending and promotions?
questions.help: Use an amount or range with a currency. Add margin, discounts, and approval limits if known. Advertising spend is separate from agency fees.
presets: Use the advertising budget already shared

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Lead follow-up and repeat business

questions.label: What makes an inquiry a qualified lead for your business?
questions.help: Choose the qualifying criteria and add any limits or cases you cannot serve.

questions.label: What should happen when a lead arrives?
questions.help: Name the owner, destination system, preferred follow-up timing, current capacity, and any appointment or sales handoff.

questions.label: What should bring people back after the first sale or interaction?
questions.help: Include recurring needs, repeat offers, cancellation reasons, or existing approved communication preferences.
presets: Help us identify a repeat offer

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Human customer handling

questions.label: Which customer conversations need help, and approximately how many arrive?
questions.help: Add the conversation types, approximate volume, and peak periods if known. “Not measured” is a valid answer.

questions.label: What may the agency handle, and what requires your approval?
questions.help: Add which tasks require your approval and any limits before work begins.

questions.label: Who takes over urgent, sensitive, or unresolved cases?
questions.help: Name the escalation person or role and availability. Requested coverage will be compared with the agreed contract.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Chatbot purpose and knowledge

questions.label: Where should a chatbot help, and which three questions or tasks should it handle first?
questions.help: Add up to three priority questions or tasks. Channel access and capabilities will be checked for the agreed scope.

questions.label: Which information can it rely on for accurate answers?
questions.help: Share approved FAQs, policies, catalog, or document links. Name who keeps the information current.

questions.label: What language and tone should it use?
options: Use the language and tone already shared
questions.help: Add customer languages or tone differences only if they differ from the earlier answers.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Chatbot actions and human handoff

questions.label: Should it only answer questions, or also take actions?
questions.help: Account and live-data actions need verified permissions and an agreed scope.

questions.label: What must it never decide or do without a person?
questions.help: Choose what needs human review and add any other boundaries.

questions.label: When should it hand over, and who should receive the conversation?
questions.help: Add who receives the conversation and any desired volume or usage-cost limit.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Automation and connected tools

questions.label: Which repetitive task or information transfer should happen automatically?
questions.placeholder: When a quote is accepted, create an invoice.
questions.help: Start with one priority from your current workflow.
presets: Help us choose the first automation

questions.label: Which tools need to be involved?
questions.help: Add tool names, versions, or plans if known.

questions.label: What should trigger the process, and what result should it produce?

fields.label: When this happens
fields.placeholder: For example: A quote is accepted

questions.help: Describe the trigger and expected result in plain language. Add approximate frequency or record volume only if known.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Data rules and failed workflows

questions.label: What information needs to move between the tools, and how quickly?
questions.help: Add how quickly information should move: instant, scheduled, manual, or undecided. Mention one-way or both ways if known.

questions.label: Which system should be trusted if records disagree?
questions.help: Name the trusted system for important customer, order, stock, or invoice records only where relevant.

questions.label: Who should be alerted when something fails, and how can work continue?
questions.help: Name the person who should receive alerts and how the team can continue manually. You may add a technical contact or public documentation link.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Moving existing data or systems

questions.label: What information or content needs to move, and from where?
questions.help: Add where each item comes from, approximate volume if known, and links to redacted examples only.

questions.label: What problems already exist in that information?
questions.help: Add who can approve cleanup.

questions.label: What must keep working while the move happens?
questions.help: Add acceptable interruption and who will verify the result.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Measurement and performance

questions.label: What do you currently measure, and where are those reports?
questions.help: Add existing report links if available. You do not need to disclose revenue.

questions.label: What is the current starting point for your main goal?
questions.placeholder: For example: Approximately 20 inquiries per month, from our CRM
questions.help: Add a metric, period, and source if available. Label estimates. We will use the goal you already shared.

questions.label: What should a useful report help you decide?
questions.help: Add what decisions the report should support, the recipient, and preferred cadence. Mention any known slow or failing user task.
presets: Help us decide what to measure

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Ongoing care and recovery

questions.label: Which systems and recurring tasks need ongoing help?
questions.help: Choose what you need help with; recurring work follows the agreed scope.

questions.label: What interruptions would affect your business most?
questions.help: Add critical operating periods, acceptable disruption or data loss, and preferred response needs if known. These are requirements to discuss.

questions.label: Who should receive alerts and approve maintenance or extra work?
questions.help: Reuse an existing contact or name the responsible person or role. Optionally add an update window and who maintains tool subscriptions.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

pages.title: Information access and protection

questions.label: Which roles should be allowed to see or change private information?
questions.help: Add what each role may see or change. Use roles and categories, without private records.

questions.label: Are there requirements for where information is stored, how long it is kept, or when it is deleted?
questions.help: Link an existing policy or name a responsible contact. Mention storage locations, retention, deletion, and AI or third-party processing restrictions where relevant.

questions.label: Who can confirm these requirements and help with incidents or access removal?
questions.help: Name the responsible person or team. You may link an existing security requirements document. Do not upload sensitive datasets.
presets: Need to appoint a responsible contact

pages.title: Policies and approvals for your business

questions.label: Which approved policies or industry requirements must the project follow?
questions.help: Add links to approved policies or requirements where available.

questions.label: Who will supply and approve missing policy text, required disclosures, or permissions?
questions.help: Name who supplies and approves policies, disclosures, and permissions. Include commercial rights for images, testimonials, designs, and other supplied assets.

questions.label: Is there any requirement that could restrict a sale, launch, campaign, or data flow?
questions.help: Mention any restriction related to your markets, special requirements, sales, launch, campaigns, or data flow.

pages.description: Share what you know. You can provide details later or ask us to help.

questions.label: Who gives final approval for scope, design, content, and launch?
questions.help: One final approver can cover all areas. Only add separate approvers where needed, with their role and email.

questions.label: Who should help review the first research and design direction?
questions.help: People or roles and availability are enough. Tell us who will consolidate feedback and any preferred review format.

questions.label: Who will run the website, customer work, and connected systems after launch?
questions.help: You can add training needs and your preferred handover format.

pages.title: Your engagement details

questions.label: Does this project summary match what you agreed with us?
questions.help: Review the summary from your approved agreement, including scope, currency, setup/recurring fees, exclusions, and separate third-party costs. If an agreement is missing, we will arrange a review.

questions.label: Are the contracting and billing details correct?
questions.help: Confirm the recorded details or correct them. If no billing record exists, give a person/legal name and billing email. Address and tax details will be requested only when needed for your contract or invoice.

questions.label: Is anything preventing you from completing the agreement or advance payment?
questions.help: Actual contract and payment status comes from agency records. Do not enter payment-card details here.

pages.description: Your approved proposal and contract provide the project summary. Selecting work in this form does not create an agreement or verify a payment.

questions.label: Should we use your project email for your client dashboard invitation?
questions.help: Confirm the project email shown here, or enter another email. The chosen address must be verified before access is granted.

questions.label: Who else should be invited to your project workspace or onboarding group?
questions.help: Add one person at a time with their name, work email, role, and requested access. Completing this form does not send invitations.

questions.label: How would you like to provide the remaining files or account access?
questions.help: We will show recorded missing items in your workspace. Add an owner and date only if known. Never enter passwords, one-time codes, or API secrets here.

pages.title: Review and submit

questions.label: Is there anything else we should understand before we begin?
questions.help: Add any preferences, concerns, or requirements not covered elsewhere.

questions.label: Are these details accurate to the best of your knowledge, and are you authorized to share them for this project?
questions.help: Review the summary and correct anything you need to. Keep estimates and unknowns clearly marked.

questions.label: Have you reviewed how your onboarding information will be used?
questions.help: Read the approved onboarding privacy information before acknowledging it. Marketing permission is separate and is not required for dashboard access.

pages.description: Check your business, goals, selected work, responsibilities, and open items. You can edit each section before submitting. Submission saves your answers; workspace activation follows verified project prerequisites.
